rv.q: While retaining the jolliness and sentimentality associated with some 170 years’ worth of stage versions (including a competitive flock that opened the year after its publication), Thorne and Warchus have polished the story’s social conscience to a restored brightness.
If your tear ducts don’t moisten multiple times during this captivating show, you must be missing the empathy gene.
An inventive ‘Christmas Carol’ tugs at the heartstrings
A Christmas Carol is a pleasant evening and easily digestible.
I only wish it were truer in spirit to the novella, which Messrs. Thorne and Warchus have watered down to the point of insipidity.
Thorne’s interest in father-son dysfunction already swallowed up the Harry Potter plays, now this voracious theme eats A Christmas Carol.
But this import from London’s Old Vic — here starring Campbell Scott — would certainly have Dickens scratching his noggin.
A Christmas Carol's quiet subversion of that holiday hysteria is precisely what makes it such a blessing for everyone this yuletide season.
Their effortless professionalism adds the spice to this heartwarming treat of a show.
And if Dickens might be thunderstruck at the Freudian undertones they’ve mined in their mission, I’d bet me last farthing that he’d approve.
In a move in line with increased efforts for better representation in the arts, two young disabled actors play Tiny Tim, Sebastian Ortiz and Jai Ram Srinivasan, both of whom have cerebral palsy.
Scott is allowed to keep some of Scrooge’s gruffer traits even after his soul-stirring transformation, which actually gives it much more credibility and emotional resonance.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this inventive but uneven adaptation, praising its intimate staging and emotional moments while questioning Jack Thorne's loose rewrite of Dickens' classic that adds darkness but loses some potency.

vs.sum: The Lyceum Theatre offers good sightlines and a charming Beaux Arts ambiance, but suffers from cramped seating and small restrooms. Ideal for intimate dramas, but patrons should be prepared for less comfort during their visit.

acc.note: 4 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. No elevator. Infrared devices available.
